config.name: Citizenship
config.title: U.S. Citizenship Test
config.subtitle: Official 2025 civics questions
config.disclaimer: Questions are from the official USCIS 2025 civics test (public domain); answer choices and explanations are ours. Not affiliated with USCIS or any government agency. Answers about current officials are not included; check uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates.

questions.text: What is the form of government of the United States?
questions.explanation: Official answers: Republic; Constitution-based federal republic; Representative democracy. (Q1)

questions.text: What is the supreme law of the land?
questions.explanation: Official answer: the (U.S.) Constitution. (Q2, 65/20 question)

questions.text: Name one thing the U.S. Constitution does.
questions.explanation: Official answers: forms the government; defines powers of government; defines the parts of government; protects the rights of the people. (Q3)

questions.text: The U.S. Constitution starts with the words "We the People." What does "We the People" mean?
questions.explanation: Official answers: self-government; popular sovereignty; consent of the governed; people should govern themselves; social contract. (Q4)

questions.text: How are changes made to the U.S. Constitution?
questions.explanation: Official answers: amendments; the amendment process. (Q5)

questions.text: What does the Bill of Rights protect?
choices: The rights of the British king
The rights of the states to leave the Union
questions.explanation: Official answers: the basic rights of Americans; the basic rights of people living in the United States. (Q6)

questions.text: How many amendments does the U.S. Constitution have?
questions.explanation: Official answer: twenty-seven (27). (Q7, 65/20 question)

questions.text: Why is the Declaration of Independence important?
choices: It set up the federal budget
It says America is free from British control
questions.explanation: Official answers: it says America is free from British control; it says all people are created equal; it identifies inherent rights; it identifies individual freedoms. (Q8)

questions.text: What founding document said the American colonies were free from Britain?
questions.explanation: Official answer: Declaration of Independence. (Q9)

questions.text: Name one important idea from the Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution.
questions.explanation: Official answers: equality; liberty; social contract; natural rights; limited government; self-government. (Q10)

questions.text: The words "Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness" are in what founding document?
questions.explanation: Official answer: Declaration of Independence. (Q11)

questions.text: What is the economic system of the United States?
questions.explanation: Official answers: capitalism; free market economy. (Q12, 65/20 question)

questions.text: What is the rule of law?
choices: Only citizens must obey the law
questions.explanation: Official answers: everyone must follow the law; leaders must obey the law; government must obey the law; no one is above the law. (Q13)

questions.text: Many documents influenced the U.S. Constitution. Name one.
questions.explanation: Official answers: Declaration of Independence; Articles of Confederation; Federalist Papers; Anti-Federalist Papers; Virginia Declaration of Rights; Fundamental Orders of Connecticut; Mayflower Compact; Iroquois Great Law of Peace. (Q14)

questions.text: There are three branches of government. Why?
choices: So one part does not become too powerful
To give the president more power
So each state has its own branch
questions.explanation: Official answers: so one part does not become too powerful; checks and balances; separation of powers. (Q15)

questions.text: Name the three branches of government.
questions.explanation: Official answers: legislative, executive, and judicial; Congress, president, and the courts. (Q16)

questions.text: The President of the United States is in charge of which branch of government?
questions.explanation: Official answer: executive branch. (Q17)

questions.text: What part of the federal government writes laws?
questions.explanation: Official answers: (U.S.) Congress; (U.S. or national) legislature; legislative branch. (Q18)

questions.text: What are the two parts of the U.S. Congress?
choices: House of Lords and House of Commons
questions.explanation: Official answer: Senate and House (of Representatives). (Q19)

questions.text: Name one power of the U.S. Congress.
questions.explanation: Official answers: writes laws; declares war; makes the federal budget. (Q20, 65/20 question)

questions.text: How many U.S. senators are there?
questions.explanation: Official answer: one hundred (100). (Q21)

questions.text: How long is a term for a U.S. senator?
questions.explanation: Official answer: six (6) years. (Q22)

questions.text: How many voting members are in the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: Official answer: four hundred thirty-five (435). (Q24)

questions.text: How long is a term for a member of the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: Official answer: two (2) years. (Q25)

questions.text: Why do U.S. representatives serve shorter terms than U.S. senators?
choices: To more closely follow public opinion
questions.explanation: Official answer: to more closely follow public opinion. (Q26)

questions.text: How many senators does each state have?
questions.explanation: Official answer: two (2). (Q27)

questions.text: Why does each state have two senators?
choices: Equal representation for small states (the Great Compromise)
Because large states asked for it
Because each state has two parties
Because the president appoints two per state
questions.explanation: Official answers: equal representation (for small states); the Great Compromise (Connecticut Compromise). (Q28)

questions.text: Who does a U.S. senator represent?
choices: Only the people who voted for them
The people of the whole country
questions.explanation: Official answers: citizens of their state; people of their state. (Q31)

questions.text: Who elects U.S. senators?
questions.explanation: Official answer: citizens from their state. (Q32)

questions.text: Who does a member of the House of Representatives represent?
questions.explanation: Official answers: citizens or people in their (congressional) district. (Q33)

questions.text: Who elects members of the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: Official answer: citizens from their (congressional) district. (Q34)

questions.text: Some states have more representatives than other states. Why?
choices: Because of the state's size in square miles
questions.explanation: Official answers: because of the state's population; because they have more people. (Q35)

questions.text: The President of the United States is elected for how many years?
questions.explanation: Official answer: four (4) years. (Q36, 65/20 question)

questions.text: The President of the United States can serve only two terms. Why?
choices: Because of the Declaration of Independence
Because of the Bill of Rights
Because the Supreme Court decided it in 1990
questions.explanation: Official answers: because of the 22nd Amendment; to keep the president from becoming too powerful. (Q37)

questions.text: If the president can no longer serve, who becomes president?
questions.explanation: Official answer: the Vice President (of the United States). (Q40)

questions.text: Name one power of the president.
questions.explanation: Official answers: signs bills into law; vetoes bills; enforces laws; Commander in Chief; chief diplomat; appoints federal judges. (Q41)

questions.text: Who is Commander in Chief of the U.S. military?
questions.explanation: Official answer: the President (of the United States). (Q42)

questions.text: Who signs bills to become laws?
questions.explanation: Official answer: the President (of the United States). (Q43)

questions.text: Who vetoes bills?
questions.explanation: Official answer: the President (of the United States). (Q44, 65/20 question)

questions.text: Who appoints federal judges?
questions.explanation: Official answer: the President (of the United States). The Senate confirms the appointments. (Q45)

questions.text: The executive branch has many parts. Name one.
questions.explanation: Official answers: President; Cabinet; federal departments and agencies. (Q46)

questions.text: What does the President's Cabinet do?
questions.explanation: Official answer: advises the President (of the United States). (Q47)

questions.text: Which of these is a Cabinet-level position?
questions.explanation: The official list includes the Attorney General, Secretary of State, Secretary of the Treasury, Secretary of Education and other department heads, plus the Vice President. (Q48)

questions.text: Why is the Electoral College important?
choices: It decides who is elected president
questions.explanation: Official answers: it decides who is elected president; it provides a compromise between the popular election of the president and congressional selection. (Q49)

questions.text: What is one part of the judicial branch?
questions.explanation: Official answers: Supreme Court; federal courts. (Q50)

questions.text: What does the judicial branch do?
choices: Decides if a law goes against the U.S. Constitution
questions.explanation: Official answers: reviews laws; explains laws; resolves disputes about the law; decides if a law goes against the (U.S.) Constitution. (Q51)

questions.text: What is the highest court in the United States?
questions.explanation: Official answer: Supreme Court. (Q52, 65/20 question)

questions.text: How many seats are on the Supreme Court?
questions.explanation: Official answer: nine (9). (Q53)

questions.text: How many Supreme Court justices are usually needed to decide a case?
questions.explanation: Official answer: five (5) — a majority of the nine justices. (Q54)

questions.text: How long do Supreme Court justices serve?
choices: Until the next president is elected
questions.explanation: Official answers: (for) life; lifetime appointment; (until) retirement. (Q55)

questions.text: Supreme Court justices serve for life. Why?
choices: To keep the same laws forever
Because they are elected by the people
Because there are not enough judges
questions.explanation: Official answers: to be independent (of politics); to limit outside (political) influence. (Q56)

questions.text: Name one power that is only for the federal government.
questions.explanation: Official answers: print paper money; mint coins; declare war; create an army; make treaties; set foreign policy. (Q58)

questions.text: Name one power that is only for the states.
questions.explanation: Official answers: provide schooling and education; provide protection (police); provide safety (fire departments); give a driver's license; approve zoning and land use. (Q59)

questions.text: What is the purpose of the 10th Amendment?
choices: Powers not given to the federal government belong to the states or to the people
It limits the president to two terms
It gives women the right to vote
questions.explanation: Official answer: it states that the powers not given to the federal government belong to the states or to the people. (Q60)

questions.text: There are four amendments to the U.S. Constitution about who can vote. Describe one of them.
choices: Citizens must pay a poll tax to vote
Citizens eighteen (18) and older can vote
questions.explanation: Official answers: citizens 18 and older can vote; you don't have to pay a poll tax to vote; any citizen can vote (women and men); a male citizen of any race can vote. (Q63)

questions.text: Who can vote in federal elections, run for federal office, and serve on a jury in the United States?
choices: Everyone living in the United States
questions.explanation: Official answers: citizens; citizens of the United States; U.S. citizens. (Q64)

questions.text: Which of these is a right of everyone living in the United States?
choices: The right to vote in federal elections
The right to serve on a jury
The right to run for president
questions.explanation: Official answers include freedom of expression, speech, assembly, religion, to petition the government, and the right to bear arms. Voting and jury service are for citizens. (Q65)

questions.text: What do we show loyalty to when we say the Pledge of Allegiance?
questions.explanation: Official answers: the United States; the flag. (Q66, 65/20 question)

questions.text: Name one promise that new citizens make in the Oath of Allegiance.
choices: Live in the same state forever
Obey the laws of the United States
questions.explanation: Official answers: give up loyalty to other countries; defend the Constitution; obey the laws of the United States; serve in the military or the nation if needed; be loyal to the United States. (Q67)

questions.text: How can people become United States citizens?
choices: Buy property in the United States
Live in the United States for one year
questions.explanation: Official answers: be born in the United States under the conditions set by the 14th Amendment; naturalize; derive citizenship under conditions set by Congress. (Q68)

questions.text: What is one example of civic participation in the United States?
questions.explanation: Official answers include: vote; run for office; join a political party; help with a campaign; join a civic or community group; contact elected officials; write to a newspaper. (Q69)

questions.text: What is one way Americans can serve their country?
questions.explanation: Official answers: vote; pay taxes; obey the law; serve in the military; run for office; work for local, state, or federal government. (Q70)

questions.text: Why is it important to pay federal taxes?
choices: It is only for business owners
It gives you the right to a passport
questions.explanation: Official answers: required by law; all people pay to fund the federal government; required by the Constitution (16th Amendment); civic duty. (Q71)

questions.text: It is important for all men age 18 through 25 to register for the Selective Service. Name one reason why.
choices: It is needed to get a passport
It makes the draft fair, if needed
questions.explanation: Official answers: required by law; civic duty; makes the draft fair, if needed. (Q72)

questions.text: The colonists came to America for many reasons. Name one.
questions.explanation: Official answers: freedom; political liberty; religious freedom; economic opportunity; escape persecution. (Q73)

questions.text: Who lived in America before the Europeans arrived?
questions.explanation: Official answers: American Indians; Native Americans. (Q74, 65/20 question)

questions.text: What group of people was taken and sold as slaves?
questions.explanation: Official answers: Africans; people from Africa. (Q75)

questions.text: What war did the Americans fight to win independence from Britain?
questions.explanation: Official answers: American Revolution; the (American) Revolutionary War; War for (American) Independence. (Q76)

questions.text: Name one reason why the Americans declared independence from Britain.
choices: Britain gave them too much self-government
questions.explanation: Official answers include: high taxes; taxation without representation; quartering of British soldiers; no self-government; Boston Massacre; Boston Tea Party; Stamp Act; Sugar Act; Townshend Acts; Intolerable Acts. (Q77)

questions.text: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?
questions.explanation: Official answer: (Thomas) Jefferson. (Q78, 65/20 question)

questions.text: When was the Declaration of Independence adopted?
questions.explanation: Official answer: July 4, 1776. (Q79)

questions.text: The American Revolution had many important events. Name one.
questions.explanation: Official answers: Bunker Hill; Declaration of Independence; Washington crossing the Delaware (Battle of Trenton); Saratoga; Valley Forge; Yorktown. (Q80)

questions.text: Which of these was one of the 13 original states?
questions.explanation: The 13 original states: New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia. (Q81 asks you to name five.)

questions.text: What founding document was written in 1787?
questions.explanation: Official answer: the (U.S.) Constitution. (Q82)

questions.text: The Federalist Papers supported the passage of the U.S. Constitution. Name one of the writers.
questions.explanation: Official answers: (James) Madison; (Alexander) Hamilton; (John) Jay; Publius. (Q83)

questions.text: Why were the Federalist Papers important?
choices: They helped people understand the U.S. Constitution
questions.explanation: Official answers: they helped people understand the Constitution; they supported passing the Constitution. (Q84)

questions.text: Benjamin Franklin is famous for many things. Name one.
choices: First president of the United States
First Postmaster General of the United States
Led the Union army in the Civil War
questions.explanation: Official answers: founded the first free public libraries; first Postmaster General; helped write the Declaration of Independence; inventor; U.S. diplomat. (Q85)

questions.text: George Washington is famous for many things. Name one.
choices: First president of the United States
questions.explanation: Official answers: "Father of Our Country"; first president; general of the Continental Army; president of the Constitutional Convention. (Q86, 65/20 question)

questions.text: Thomas Jefferson is famous for many things. Name one.
choices: First president of the United States
Doubled the size of the United States (Louisiana Purchase)
questions.explanation: Official answers: writer of the Declaration of Independence; third president; Louisiana Purchase; first Secretary of State; founded the University of Virginia; Virginia Statute on Religious Freedom. (Q87)

questions.text: James Madison is famous for many things. Name one.
choices: First president of the United States
Led the country during World War II
questions.explanation: Official answers: "Father of the Constitution"; fourth president; president during the War of 1812; one of the writers of the Federalist Papers. (Q88)

questions.text: Alexander Hamilton is famous for many things. Name one.
choices: Third president of the United States
questions.explanation: Official answers: first Secretary of the Treasury; one of the writers of the Federalist Papers; helped establish the First Bank of the United States; aide to George Washington; member of the Continental Congress. (Q89)

questions.text: What territory did the United States buy from France in 1803?
questions.explanation: Official answers: Louisiana Territory; Louisiana. (Q90)

questions.text: Name one war fought by the United States in the 1800s.
questions.explanation: Official answers: War of 1812; Mexican-American War; Civil War; Spanish-American War. (Q91)

questions.text: Name the U.S. war between the North and the South.
questions.explanation: Official answer: the Civil War. (Q92)

questions.text: The Civil War had many important events. Name one.
questions.explanation: Official answers: Fort Sumter; Emancipation Proclamation; Vicksburg; Gettysburg; Sherman's March; surrender at Appomattox; Antietam/Sharpsburg; Lincoln was assassinated. (Q93)

questions.text: Abraham Lincoln is famous for many things. Name one.
choices: First president of the United States
questions.explanation: Official answers: freed the slaves (Emancipation Proclamation); saved the Union; led the U.S. during the Civil War; 16th president; delivered the Gettysburg Address. (Q94, 65/20 question)

questions.text: What did the Emancipation Proclamation do?
choices: Freed the slaves in the Confederate states
Gave women the right to vote
questions.explanation: Official answers: freed the slaves; freed slaves in the Confederacy / Confederate states / most Southern states. (Q95)

questions.text: What U.S. war ended slavery?
questions.explanation: Official answer: the Civil War. (Q96)

questions.text: What amendment says all persons born or naturalized in the United States, and subject to the jurisdiction thereof, are U.S. citizens?
questions.explanation: Official answer: 14th Amendment. (Q97)

questions.text: When did all men get the right to vote?
questions.explanation: Official answers: after the Civil War; during Reconstruction; with the 15th Amendment; 1870. (Q98)

questions.text: Name one leader of the women's rights movement in the 1800s.
questions.explanation: Official answers: Susan B. Anthony; Elizabeth Cady Stanton; Sojourner Truth; Harriet Tubman; Lucretia Mott; Lucy Stone. (Q99)

questions.text: Name one war fought by the United States in the 1900s.
questions.explanation: Official answers: World War I; World War II; Korean War; Vietnam War; (Persian) Gulf War. (Q100)

questions.text: Why did the United States enter World War I?
choices: To force Iraq out of Kuwait
To stop the spread of communism
Because Germany attacked U.S. civilian ships
questions.explanation: Official answers: because Germany attacked U.S. (civilian) ships; to support the Allied Powers; to oppose the Central Powers. (Q101)

questions.text: When did all women get the right to vote?
questions.explanation: Official answers: 1920; after World War I; with the 19th Amendment. (Q102)

questions.text: What was the Great Depression?
choices: The longest economic recession in modern history
A period of very fast economic growth
A war between the North and the South
questions.explanation: Official answer: longest economic recession in modern history. (Q103)

questions.text: When did the Great Depression start?
choices: With the stock market crash of 1929
questions.explanation: Official answers: the Great Crash (1929); stock market crash of 1929. (Q104)

questions.text: Who was president during the Great Depression and World War II?
questions.explanation: Official answer: (Franklin) Roosevelt. (Q105)

questions.text: Why did the United States enter World War II?
choices: Britain declared war on the United States
questions.explanation: Official answers: (bombing of) Pearl Harbor; to support the Allied Powers; to oppose the Axis Powers (Germany, Italy, and Japan). (Q106)

questions.text: Dwight Eisenhower is famous for many things. Name one.
questions.explanation: Official answers: general during World War II; president at the end of the Korean War; 34th president; signed the Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956. (Q107)

questions.text: Who was the United States' main rival during the Cold War?
questions.explanation: Official answers: Soviet Union; USSR; Russia. (Q108)

questions.text: During the Cold War, what was one main concern of the United States?
questions.explanation: Official answers: communism; nuclear war. (Q109)

questions.text: Why did the United States enter the Korean War?
choices: Because of the attack on Pearl Harbor
To stop the spread of communism
questions.explanation: Official answer: to stop the spread of communism. (Q110)

questions.text: Why did the United States enter the Vietnam War?
choices: To stop the spread of communism
questions.explanation: Official answer: to stop the spread of communism. (Q111)

questions.text: What did the civil rights movement do?
questions.explanation: Official answer: fought to end racial discrimination. (Q112)

questions.text: Martin Luther King, Jr. is famous for many things. Name one.
choices: Led the army in World War II
questions.explanation: Official answers: fought for civil rights; worked for equality for all Americans; worked so people would "not be judged by the color of their skin, but by the content of their character." (Q113, 65/20 question)

questions.text: Why did the United States enter the Persian Gulf War?
choices: To force the Iraqi military from Kuwait
To buy oil fields in Mexico
To stop the Soviet Union in Korea
questions.explanation: Official answer: to force the Iraqi military from Kuwait. (Q114)

questions.text: What major event happened on September 11, 2001 in the United States?
choices: A man landed on the moon
questions.explanation: Official answers: terrorists attacked the United States; planes were crashed into the World Trade Center, the Pentagon and a field in Pennsylvania. (Q115, 65/20 question)

questions.text: Name one U.S. military conflict after the September 11, 2001 attacks.
questions.explanation: Official answers: (Global) War on Terror; War in Afghanistan; War in Iraq. (Q116)

questions.text: Name one American Indian tribe in the United States.
questions.explanation: The official list includes Apache, Cherokee, Cheyenne, Navajo, Sioux, Seminole, Mohawk, Hopi and others. The Aztec and Inca lived in Mexico and South America; the Maori in New Zealand. (Q117)

questions.text: Name one example of an American innovation.
questions.explanation: Official answers: light bulb; automobile; skyscrapers; airplane; assembly line; landing on the moon; integrated circuit. (Q118)

questions.text: What is the capital of the United States?
questions.explanation: Official answer: Washington, D.C. (Q119)

questions.text: Where is the Statue of Liberty?
questions.explanation: Official answers: New York (Harbor); Liberty Island. Also acceptable: New Jersey, near New York City, on the Hudson River. (Q120)

questions.text: Why does the flag have 13 stripes?
questions.explanation: Official answers: because there were 13 original colonies; the stripes represent the original colonies. (Q121, 65/20 question)

questions.text: Why does the flag have 50 stars?
questions.explanation: Official answers: one star for each state; each star represents a state; there are 50 states. (Q122)

questions.text: What is the name of the national anthem?
questions.explanation: Official answer: The Star-Spangled Banner. (Q123)

questions.text: The Nation's first motto was "E Pluribus Unum." What does that mean?
questions.explanation: Official answers: out of many, one; we all become one. (Q124)

questions.text: What is Independence Day?
choices: A holiday to honor soldiers who died in service
A holiday to celebrate the harvest
A holiday to celebrate U.S. independence from Britain
questions.explanation: Official answers: a holiday to celebrate U.S. independence (from Britain); the country's birthday. (Q125)

questions.text: Which of these is a national U.S. holiday?
questions.explanation: Official national holidays: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Presidents Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day. (Q126 asks for three, 65/20 question)

questions.text: What is Memorial Day?
choices: A holiday to celebrate the New Year
A holiday to honor all workers
A holiday to honor soldiers who died in military service
questions.explanation: Official answer: a holiday to honor soldiers who died in military service. (Q127)

questions.text: What is Veterans Day?
choices: A holiday to honor people who have served in the U.S. military
A holiday to celebrate the harvest
A holiday to celebrate the Constitution
questions.explanation: Official answers: a holiday to honor people in the (U.S.) military; a holiday to honor people who have served. (Q128)
